nodes.label: Across a 43% growth-rate change (minimal 0.90/h -> rich 1.28/h), v2ecoli's or...
nodes.statement: Across a 43% growth-rate change (minimal 0.90/h -> rich 1.28/h), v2ecoli's origins-per-cell rise from 2.43 to 4.21 (slope +4.60 per 1/h) while the mass per origin stays ~constant (648 -> 696 fg, 7.1%). This is the Cooper-Helmstetter / Donachie growth law emerging from the mechanism, not imposed: faster growth compresses the doubling time below C+D, forcing overlapping rounds of replication at a fixed initiation mass. The coupling runs through ppGpp, which is 4.1x higher in the slow condition (74.8 vs 18.3) with RelA correspondingly elevated.

nodes.label: Two results, one landed fix. (1) The carbon-quality ladder crashed on the ace...
nodes.statement: Two results, one landed fix. (1) The carbon-quality ladder crashed on the acetate/succinate conditions with a spurious "Homeostatic target must be non-negative (-1.5e-6 for BIOTIN[c])" — pure floating-point noise from the ParCa fit. A small, principled correction to modular_fba.py clamps such numerical-noise negatives to 0 (a homeostatic target is a concentration, and -1.5e-6 is zero within tolerance), leaving genuinely-negative targets to still error. This is a real, landed model-robustness improvement. (2) With the conditions unblocked, v2ecoli reproduces the Scott et al. 2010 ribosome growth law: ribosome concentration rises monotonically with growth rate across the carbon ladder — acetate 1.42, succinate 1.87, glucose 20.8, +AA 21.2 (acetate/succinate ribosome values independently re-read from the run parquets). This resolves the caveat Arc 1 flagged (that amino-acid supplementation left ribosome_conc flat on the R-line): on the carbon-limitation C-line the ribosomal fraction does track growth, as biology requires.

nodes.label: v2ecoli reproduces the qualitative Bremer-Dennis growth law: the RNA/protein ...
nodes.statement: v2ecoli reproduces the qualitative Bremer-Dennis growth law: the RNA/protein mass ratio rises with growth rate, from 0.310 at mu 0.90/h (minimal glucose) to 0.318 at mu 1.28/h (amino-acid-rich), a positive slope of +0.021 per (1/h). The direction is correct and emerges from the native mass balance. The magnitude is shallow — only a ~3% rise in RNA/protein for a 43% rise in growth rate — where the classic law predicts a steeper climb. This is consistent with the two conditions spanning an amino-acid-supply (R-line) axis rather than a carbon-quality (C-line) series: supplying amino acids raises growth without demanding proportionally more ribosomes. The C-line test (where ribosomal fraction tracks growth steeply) is carried by the sibling study mcs-07, which shows ribosome concentration climbing across an acetate/succinate/glucose carbon ladder.

nodes.label: The v2ecoli baseline builds 0.816 gDW biomass per gram of glucose (1.84x the ...
nodes.statement: The v2ecoli baseline builds 0.816 gDW biomass per gram of glucose (1.84x the measured band, 1.52x the first-principles ceiling) while barely respiring (O2:glucose 0.137, RQ 2.94 — impossible for pure aerobic respiration). Prior work SCOPED the fix to maintenance ATP (GAM/NGAM) and respiratory capacity. This study tests that directly and REFUTES it: scaling GAM to 5x and NGAM to 10x (83.9 mmol/gDW/h, an order of magnitude above the Feist iAF1260 literature value, and verified to reach the FBA via model.ngam) moves biomass yield less than 2% and leaves O2 uptake and growth essentially unchanged. The FBA is insensitive to the maintenance-ATP bound because ATP is already over-supplied: the cell meets any maintenance demand from a surplus, so the defect cannot be in ATP DEMAND. It is in ATP SUPPLY — the ATP-generation stoichiometry (a too-high effective P/O ratio / an over-efficient or short-circuited electron-transport chain), which also explains why the cell makes ATP with almost no O2 (RQ ~3). This advances the prior investigation from 'energetic defect, fix scoped to maintenance' to 'energetic defect, maintenance fix falsified, defect localized to oxidative-phosphorylation stoichiometry.'

nodes.label: decision/derived-mcs-02-metabolism-energy-balance-fl0
Auditing the baseline FBA solution shows the root of the energetic defect: AT...
nodes.statement: Auditing the baseline FBA solution shows the root of the energetic defect: ATP synthase (ATPSYN-RXN) carries ZERO forward (synthesis) flux and 7.48 units of REVERSE (hydrolysis) flux — it is running backwards, spending ATP to pump protons rather than making ATP from respiration. The cell therefore makes essentially no ATP by oxidative phosphorylation (respiratory P/O ~ 0), consistent with its near-absent O2 use (0.89 mmol/gDW/h) and impossible RQ (2.94). ATP is instead over-produced by substrate-level phosphorylation and the surplus is dissipated through the reverse ATP synthase. This explains Arc 2's central puzzle — why raising maintenance ATP did nothing: the cell already has an ATP surplus it is actively throwing away, so demanding more of it just changes how much is dissipated, not the carbon/O2 flux. Both NADH dehydrogenase routes are present in the reaction set (NADH-DEHYDROG-A-RXN carries a small flux ~0.009; NADH-DEHYDROGENASE-QUINONE-RXN is idle). Correcting the behaviour (constraining ATP synthase to net-forward operation under aerobiosis, matching genome-scale iAF1260) is the principled fix, but it is a reaction-bound change that can render the FBA infeasible, so it is flagged for a dedicated pass rather than applied speculatively here.

nodes.label: decision/derived-mcs-05-etc-stoichiometry-fix-fl0
Applying, refining and INTEGRATING the fix the diagnostic pointed to corrects...
nodes.statement: Applying, refining and INTEGRATING the fix the diagnostic pointed to corrects the energetic defect and lands biomass yield squarely in the measured band. Capping ATP synthase's reverse (ATPase) flux forces net-forward (respiratory) operation. A raw cap of 0 over-shot (yield 0.268, just below band, over-respiring at the glucose-uptake cap); sweeping the cap (0->0.268, 4->0.356, 5->0.435) and calibrating it to 4.5 CENTRES the yield. The correction is then committed to the model (metabolism.py: atp_synthase_reverse_cap, applied before every FBA solve) and validated natively: biomass yield falls from 0.816 to 0.390 gDW/g glucose — from 1.84x OVER the band to the middle of the measured 0.355-0.444 band, flipping the graded physiology.biomass_yield axis from first_principles_violation to passing. RQ falls from an impossible 2.94 to a physiological 1.11 and growth is PRESERVED (0.956 -> 0.974/h) — both HELD-OUT (only the yield-centering cap was tuned). O2 uptake rises 0.89 -> 16.9 (respiration ON) and, tellingly, acetate overflow now appears (secretion 13.4 mmol/gDW/h) — the model spontaneously reproduces the aerobic overflow of Basan 2015 once it actually respires. The FBA stays feasible throughout. This fully closes the gap->fix->validate loop the Arc 2 thread opened: the maintenance-ATP hypothesis was refuted (mcs-02), the true cause localized (reverse ATP synthase), and the correction applied, refined, integrated and held-out-validated.

nodes.label: A regression check confirms the ETC fix corrects biomass yield WITHOUT collat...
nodes.statement: A regression check confirms the ETC fix corrects biomass yield WITHOUT collateral damage. A 3-generation basal run with the fix as the default was compared axis-by-axis to the identical pre-fix run (Arc 1's basal). Every non-metabolic axis holds within a few percent: growth rate 0.896 -> 0.883/h (-1.5%), interdivision time 43-47 min (unchanged), cell mass 1575 -> 1608 fg (+2%), origins/cell 2.43 -> 2.47, initiation mass 648 -> 652 fg, ribosome concentration 20.8 -> 21.5, and macromolecular composition is essentially unchanged (protein fraction +3.6%, RNA fraction +2.7%, DNA fraction -0.3%, RNA/protein -0.9%). The run stays feasible across all divisions. The only material shifts are metabolism-adjacent signaling (ppGpp 74.8 -> 68.2, -9%; RelA rises off a tiny base) — plausible now that the cell respires rather than fermenting. So the fix improves the graded biomass_yield and RQ axes while leaving growth, the cell cycle, replication and composition within band: no regression.

nodes.label: Across a 6-seed ensemble, v2ecoli's interdivision-time coefficient of variati...
nodes.statement: Across a 6-seed ensemble, v2ecoli's interdivision-time coefficient of variation is 7% (mean generation time 49 min), well below the 10-30% measured in single-cell E. coli. The heterogeneity is real but slow to develop: sibling lineages started from different seeds are IDENTICAL in division time at generation 2 (CV 0.000), diverging only to 3% by generation 3 and 5% by generation 4. Birth mass spans just 309-358 fg (CV ~4%), too narrow to resolve whether the cell is an adder, sizer or timer — and that narrowness is itself the signature of under-dispersion. The whole-cell model is more deterministic / synchronized than real cells, consistent with its use of expected (mean) rates in many processes rather than fully stochastic kinetics. Closing this gap is a structural modeling change (adding stochastic mechanisms), not a parameter tweak, so it is flagged rather than applied here.

nodes.label: decision/derived-mcs-03-single-cell-heterogeneity-fl0
Enabling the stochastic D-period (Normal(1.0,0.15) x D_period, seeded, floore...
nodes.statement: Enabling the stochastic D-period (Normal(1.0,0.15) x D_period, seeded, floored, routed into the active division trigger in chromosome_replication.py) raises the ensemble interdivision-time CV from 0.068 (noise-OFF, 18 cells) to 0.115 (noise-ON, 18 cells) — from below the biological band into it (0.10-0.30, Taheri-Araghi 2015). The mean generation time is approximately preserved (48.8 -> 46.7 min, -4.4%): variance was added with only a small mean shift, which is attributable to the 0.5x floor clamp's asymmetry rather than the noise. The fix is default-off (cv=0 leaves the committed baseline byte-identical), so it is available as an opt-in fidelity setting without changing baseline results.

nodes.label: Moving from minimal glucose to amino-acid-rich medium shifts every scale of t...
nodes.statement: Moving from minimal glucose to amino-acid-rich medium shifts every scale of the whole-cell model coherently: the stringent-response alarmone ppGpp drops 4.1-fold (74.8->18.3), the number of replication origins rises from 2.4 to 4.2, the single-cell growth rate rises from 0.90 to 1.28/h, and glucose uptake rises from 6.5 to 9.9 mmol/gDW/h. A single environmental change propagates from a molecular signal up through the cell cycle and metabolism — the integrated multiscale behavior the investigation set out to demonstrate. (Metabolism's ABSOLUTE respiration remains defective per Arc 2 — at rich medium O2 uptake collapses to ~0 — so the metabolic READOUT used here is glucose uptake, which is physiological, rather than the pathological respiratory quotient.)

nodes.label: The Arc-1 cross-condition effects survive multi-seed resampling with non-over...
nodes.statement: The Arc-1 cross-condition effects survive multi-seed resampling with non-overlapping 95% confidence intervals: origins/cell 2.38+/-0.03 vs 3.55+/-0.004, ppGpp 72.2+/-4.8 vs 21.7+/-1.8, growth 0.85+/-0.03 vs 1.27+/-0.04/h across 6 seeds each. The single-seed point estimates behind mcs-01 and the capstone were not flukes; the effects are an order of magnitude larger than the seed-to-seed scatter. nodes.label: Pooling the 6-seed basal ensemble, the interdivision-time CV is 0.048 (11 cel...
nodes.statement: Pooling the 6-seed basal ensemble, the interdivision-time CV is 0.048 (11 cells) — below and consistent with the single-seed 0.070, so the Arc-3 under-dispersion (CV well below the biological 10-30% band) is a robust structural property, not a single-seed artifact. With the larger ensemble the adder regression slope resolves to ~0 (added mass independent of birth mass), i.e. the model DOES show adder-like size homeostasis even though its timing CV is too tight — a distinction mcs-03 could not make with 18 cells. This sharpens the mcs-06 target: add timing variance without disturbing the (correct) adder behaviour.

nodes.label: The held-out acetate-overflow-onset check falsifies the mcs-05 fix AS CHARACT...
nodes.statement: The held-out acetate-overflow-onset check falsifies the mcs-05 fix AS CHARACTERIZED. Run with the committed reverse-cap (4.5) on, the cell does not respire (acetate 0, RQ 2.85, yield 0.819) — the overflow the fix should produce is absent. A controlled two-path comparison at the SAME cap shows why: the explicit solve-wrapping path reaches a respiring optimum (yield 0.395, RQ 1.10, matching mcs-05), while the committed-default path reaches a non-respiring optimum (reverse flux pinned at the cap 4.5, forward ATP synthase 0). Capping the REVERSE direction to 4.5 permits but does not FORCE forward (respiratory) operation, so the FBA optimum — and the biomass yield — is solve-path dependent. The ATP-synthase-in-reverse DIAGNOSIS (mcs-05 finding 1) stands; the one-parameter reverse-cap FIX is not robust and must be reformulated to reward/force forward ATP synthase, not merely bound the reverse.

nodes.label: decision/derived-mcs-11-etc-heldout-and-downshift-fl0
Following the mcs-11 non-reproducibility, the ETC fix was systematically refo...
nodes.statement: Following the mcs-11 non-reproducibility, the ETC fix was systematically reformulated to FORCE forward respiration. Three formulations were tested on the real composite: (1) lower-bounding the FORWARD ATP-synthase reaction alone does NOTHING — the reverse flux rises to match it (a futile cycle), so net stays reverse-hydrolysis and yield stays 0.815; (2) forcing net-forward via reverse=0 gives robust respiration (RQ 1.22, O2 up, acetate overflow, 0 infeasible) but yield 0.268, BELOW the band, with ATP synthase bypassed; (3) forcing net-forward THROUGH ATP synthase (forward-min + reverse=0) reaches the band (yield 0.41) ONLY at forward-min=12, where growth blows up to 1.48/h (vs the physiological ~0.97) with non-physiological O2/acetate (O2 ~104). Across the sweep, yield and growth rise together, so an in-band yield REQUIRES growth ~1.5. Conclusion: no ATP-synthase FLUX BOUND simultaneously forces respiration, reproduces the measured yield, and preserves growth. The defect is STOICHIOMETRIC — the effective oxidative-phosphorylation P/O ratio (ATP per O2 / per glucose) is mis-set — and the principled correction is a reaction-stoichiometry change (H+/ATP coupling, ETC proton pumping), NOT a flux bound. This localizes the Arc-2 defect one level deeper than mcs-05 and explains WHY the reverse-cap was degenerate: a flux bound cannot fix a stoichiometric error.

nodes.label: Tracing the ATP-supply defect to its root: the model synthesizes ATP via ATP ...
nodes.statement: Tracing the ATP-supply defect to its root: the model synthesizes ATP via ATP synthase (flux ~7.5) while consuming almost no O2 (~0.9), so the proton-motive force is NOT respiratory. A per-reaction proton-balance audit finds the source — a succinate/proton FUTILE CYCLE: TRANS-RXN-300 exports succinate with 3 H+ (SUC[c]+3H+[c]->SUC[p]+3H+[p]) and TRANS-RXN0-517 re-imports it with 2 H+ (SUC[p]+2H+[p]->SUC[c]+2H+[c]); run together (~18 flux each) succinate is unchanged but 1 net H+ is pumped cytoplasm->periplasm per turn — proton-motive force generated for FREE, thermodynamically impossible. That free PMF drives ATP synthase, so the cell makes ATP without respiring (yield 0.82, RQ 2.94, no acetate overflow). Two controls prove this is the mechanism and that it is SYSTEMIC: (1) changing the ATP-synthase H+/ATP ratio (4->3->6) has NO effect on yield or O2 (rules out the P/O ratio); (2) blocking TRANS-RXN-300 does NOT fix it (yield stays 0.817) — the FBA reroutes to another free-proton pump (TRANS-RXN0-601 (reverse), a direct H+/H+ translocator, ~22 H+). The defect is a KNOWN class of genome-scale-FBA artifact: the LP has no thermodynamic loop-law constraints, so internal free-energy-generating proton cycles are feasible. The principled correction is LOOPLESS / THERMODYNAMIC FBA (loop-law constraints forbidding free-energy-generating internal cycles) — a solver-level change, not a parameter, stoichiometry, or single-reaction flux bound.
